blocks.prompt: 1 (i) A particle is moving in a straight line and its acceleration is given by \(a = 2t - 7\). Find velocity \(v\) in terms of \(t\) if \(v = 10\) m/sec, when \(t = 0\).
blocks.explanation:
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, \(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\), so the data give a first-order differential equation for \(v\).
The right side has only \(t\), so it is separable: integrate once.
Plan: write \(\frac{dv}{dt} = 2t - 7\), integrate, then use \(v(0) = 10\) for the constant.
steps:
Given: \(a = 2t - 7\); \(v = 10\) m/sec when \(t = 0\).
To find: \(v\) in terms of \(t\).
Method: \(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\). Separate the variables, integrate, and fix the constant of integration with the initial condition.

Write the differential equation
\[\dfrac{dv}{dt} = 2t - 7\]
\[dv = (2t - 7)\,dt\]
Why: acceleration is the derivative of velocity with respect to time.

Integrate both sides
\[\int dv = \int (2t - 7)\,dt\]
\[v = t^{2} - 7t + C\]
Why: \(\int 2t\,dt = t^{2}\) and \(\int 7\,dt = 7t\) (power rule).

Use \(v(0) = 10\)
\[10 = 0 - 0 + C\]
\[C = 10\]
\[v = t^{2} - 7t + 10\]
Why: at \(t = 0\) the terms with \(t\) vanish, so \(C\) is the starting velocity.

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}(t^{2} - 7t + 10) = 2t - 7 \;\checkmark\]
\(v(0) = 10 \;\checkmark\)
Why: the derivative gives back the acceleration and the initial condition holds.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) A particle is moving in a straight line and its acceleration is given by \(a = 2t - 7\). Find distance \(s\) in terms of \(t\) if \(s = 0\) m [printed as 0 m/sec], when \(t = 0\).
blocks.explanation:
Velocity is the rate of change of distance, \(v = \frac{ds}{dt}\). From part (i), \(\frac{ds}{dt} = t^{2} - 7t + 10\).
Plan: integrate once more and use \(s(0) = 0\).
steps:
Given: \(v = t^{2} - 7t + 10\) (from part (i)); \(s = 0\) when \(t = 0\).
To find: \(s\) in terms of \(t\).
Method: \(v = \frac{ds}{dt}\) is again separable; integrate and fix the constant with \(s(0) = 0\).

Write the differential equation
\[\dfrac{ds}{dt} = t^{2} - 7t + 10\]
\[ds = (t^{2} - 7t + 10)\,dt\]
Why: velocity is the derivative of distance with respect to time.

Integrate both sides
\[\int ds = \int (t^{2} - 7t + 10)\,dt\]
\[s = \dfrac{t^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{7t^{2}}{2} + 10t + C_2\]
Why: power rule \(\int t^{n}\,dt = \frac{t^{n+1}}{n+1}\) term by term.

Use \(s(0) = 0\)
\[0 = 0 - 0 + 0 + C_2\]
\[C_2 = 0\]
\[s = \dfrac{1}{3}t^{3} - \dfrac{7}{2}t^{2} + 10t\]
Why: every term with t vanishes at t = 0.

Check
\[\dfrac{ds}{dt} = t^{2} - 7t + 10 = v \;\checkmark\]
\(s(0) = 0 \;\checkmark\)
Why: differentiating gives back the velocity of part (i).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints the second condition as '\(s = 0\) m/sec, when \(t = 0\)'. m/sec is a unit of velocity; distance is measured in metres, so it should read \(s = 0\) m when \(t = 0\). The working and the answer are not affected.
